packs.title: Marble, Brick and Open Sky
packs.promise: Find another Athens in a painted gesture, an industrial outline and a roof full of light.

q.s: Collect three gestures from a coloured band above the columns.
st: Find the painted band behind the front columns in the official facade image or from a permitted exterior viewpoint. It is fine to use the image to see the details.
Collect three different gestures: a turned head, an arm position and the direction of a body. Describe what each gesture could be doing without needing to name the figures.
Put your three observations in an order that suggests listening, answering and waiting. Save the collection; the order is your interpretation, not a historical claim.

q.s: Make a small imagined exhibition from a museum’s exterior.
st: Choose two exterior details you can comfortably see, or use the official building photograph: a surface texture, an opening, an edge or a contrast of light and shade.
Invent two small artworks for an exhibition of your own. Give each a title and one sentence saying what it would be made from, inspired by one chosen detail.
Save the two titles and material ideas. You do not need to make the artworks or describe a real exhibition.

q.s: Make a return plan before your small outing ends.
st: Choose a destination that suits your day. From a comfortable stopped place, check the current OASA route information and identify a possible return journey from Kerameikos.
Note the line or connection, what you would check before departure, and where you could stop comfortably if you needed a break. Do not record your home address in a shared note.
Make a second plan for staying in the square or returning another way if the first route does not suit you. Save both plans. Taking a ride, entering the station or covering a distance is optional.

packs.title: Stone Frames and Garden Time
packs.promise: Find an Athens story in the space between a stone edge and a moving leaf.

q.t: Three Ways to Catch the Light
q.s: Collect contrasts outside the Acropolis Museum.
st: Choose a public viewpoint outside the Acropolis Museum with part of its modern exterior visible. Keep queues and entrances clear.
Find three different ways the scene handles light: a reflection in glass, a solid surface and a shadow or darker recess.
Give each one a word for its texture or mood. Cloudy light is enough; a bright reflection is not necessary.
Save the three observations and choose the contrast that most changes the way you see the building.

q.s: Give an everyday Plaka view a title of your own.
st: Choose a roomy public stopping place near Filomousou Eterias Square. Look at an exterior facade and an edge of the street around it.
Pick two visible colours: one from the building and one from paving, a shutter or another fixed street detail.
Write a short title for this view using both colours, then add a single sentence that gives the scene a mood.
Save your title, sentence and the two details that supplied the colours.

q.s: Find symmetry and one small difference at Zappeion.
st: Choose a public viewpoint in front of Zappeion Megaron that shows its central entrance and part of each wing. Stay beyond event boundaries.
Find two pairs of repeated features on opposite sides of the centre, such as columns, windows or roof edges.
Look for one difference created by light, planting or the viewing angle. It need not be a difference in the architecture itself.
Save the two pairs and the difference as a three-part description of the facade.
